label: Ad Hominem
topic: Should the city fund free bus travel for students?
snippet: You cannot be trusted on transport at all — you have never used a bus in your life and you failed your economics exam.
why: Attacks the speaker's experience and exam record instead of the bus policy.

label: Ad Hominem
topic: Should school days start later for teenagers?
snippet: My opponent wants a later start, but he was late to this debate himself, so his point about sleep is worthless.
why: Uses the opponent's punctuality as a reason to dismiss the argument.

label: Ad Hominem
topic: Should companies be allowed to use AI in hiring?
snippet: Anyone who supports AI hiring is clearly a technophile who does not care about workers, so their concerns should be dismissed.
why: Labels supporters rather than answering the hiring question.

label: Ad Hominem
topic: Should the voting age be lowered to sixteen?
snippet: The other side is a group of retirees with no stake in schools, which is why their objection to sixteen-year-olds voting should be ignored.
why: Rejects the objection because of who makes it, not what it says.

label: Ad Hominem
topic: Is a four-day work week better for everyone?
snippet: You can dismiss her productivity figures — she is a consultant who has never run a shift in a warehouse.
why: Discredits the person instead of examining the figures.

label: Straw Man
topic: Should cities ban cars from their centres?
snippet: My opponent wants cleaner air, which really means banning every car, closing the shops and forcing families to walk ten miles to hospital.
why: Expands a clean-air argument into a caricature nobody proposed.

label: Straw Man
topic: Should schools ban phones?
snippet: The other side says phones distract students; what they actually want is to search every child's bag every morning.
why: Replaces the distraction argument with an invented bag-search policy.

label: Straw Man
topic: Should the government cap rent increases?
snippet: Supporters of rent caps want to abolish private property and put every landlord on a state payroll.
why: Attributes abolition of property to supporters of a rent cap.

label: Straw Man
topic: Should AI be allowed to grade essays?
snippet: Critics of AI grading want teachers to spend every evening marking by hand and never use a computer again.
why: Turns a fairness objection into a technophobic demand.

label: Straw Man
topic: Should the voting age be lowered to sixteen?
snippet: Advocates for a lower voting age apparently think twelve-year-olds should also vote and run for parliament.
why: Invents a much wider proposal to make the case look absurd.

label: False Dilemma
topic: Should cities ban cars from their centres?
snippet: Either we ban cars from the centre this year or our children will keep breathing poison. There is no third option.
why: Rules out milder measures between a ban and poisoned air.

label: False Dilemma
topic: Should social platforms verify every user?
snippet: We either verify every account with an ID or the internet becomes a lawless playground. Pick one.
why: Presents two extremes and excludes narrower verification rules.

label: False Dilemma
topic: Is a four-day work week better for everyone?
snippet: A company can either move to four days or accept that its staff will burn out. Nothing in between will work.
why: Denies any middle option such as flexible hours.

label: False Dilemma
topic: Should schools teach financial literacy?
snippet: If we do not make money management a compulsory subject, an entire generation will end up bankrupt.
why: Frames the choice as compulsory lessons or bankruptcy.

label: False Dilemma
topic: Should the voting age be lowered to sixteen?
snippet: You are either for young people having a voice or you are against democracy.
why: Collapses every objection into being against democracy.

label: Slippery Slope
topic: Should schools ban phones?
snippet: If we confiscate phones in class today, schools will start searching bags next term, then monitoring every message students send.
why: Chains unrelated outcomes from one phone rule.

label: Slippery Slope
topic: Should the government cap rent increases?
snippet: Cap rents this year and landlords will sell everything, the rental market will vanish, and families will end up on the street.
why: Unstoppable chain from a rent cap to homelessness.

label: Slippery Slope
topic: Should AI be allowed to grade essays?
snippet: Let a machine mark one essay and soon no teacher will be employed, and students will be taught entirely by software.
why: One marking task is said to lead to replacing all teaching.

label: Slippery Slope
topic: Should cities ban cars from their centres?
snippet: Close one street to cars and the next step is banning all vehicles, then banning travel outside your own neighbourhood.
why: Escalates a single street closure into a travel ban.

label: Slippery Slope
topic: Should social platforms verify every user?
snippet: Require an ID once and the state will soon demand ID for every website, every message and every search.
why: Predicts total monitoring from one verification rule.

label: Appeal to Authority
topic: Is a four-day work week better for everyone?
snippet: A famous footballer says four-day weeks changed his life, so the policy must work for every workplace.
why: Sports fame is offered as proof about workplace policy.

label: Appeal to Authority
topic: Should schools ban phones?
snippet: A billionaire tech founder said phones are destroying childhood, so his view settles the debate.
why: Wealth and tech success do not settle a schools question.

label: Appeal to Authority
topic: Should the government cap rent increases?
snippet: A Nobel laureate in physics endorsed rent caps, so the economics must be sound.
why: Expertise in physics does not establish housing economics.

label: Appeal to Authority
topic: Should AI be allowed to grade essays?
snippet: An award-winning novelist says AI cannot understand writing, therefore no AI grader can ever be fair.
why: A novelist's opinion is treated as decisive evidence about grading systems.

label: Appeal to Authority
topic: Should the city fund free bus travel for students?
snippet: The mayor's brother, who runs a taxi firm, says free buses are a mistake, so we should trust him on transport.
why: An interested party's status is offered instead of evidence.

label: Circular Reasoning
topic: Should cities ban cars from their centres?
snippet: The ban is fair because it is the just thing to do.
why: Fairness restates the conclusion without support.

label: Circular Reasoning
topic: Should social platforms verify every user?
snippet: Verification is necessary because without it the platform would not be able to verify anyone.
why: Necessity is justified by restating the need.

label: Circular Reasoning
topic: Should school days start later for teenagers?
snippet: A later start is better for teenagers because waking later is what is best for them.
why: Both halves say the same thing.

label: Circular Reasoning
topic: Should the government cap rent increases?
snippet: Rent caps help tenants because they make renting more affordable for tenants.
why: Affordability is the claim, not the reason for it.

label: Circular Reasoning
topic: Should AI be allowed to grade essays?
snippet: AI grading is unreliable because you cannot rely on it.
why: Unreliability is offered as its own explanation.

label: Hasty Generalization
topic: Should cities ban cars from their centres?
snippet: Two of my neighbours sold their cars after the trial, so the whole city has given up driving.
why: Two households are treated as the whole city.

label: Hasty Generalization
topic: Should schools ban phones?
snippet: My cousin's class got better marks after the phone ban, so bans raise results in every school in the country.
why: One class is generalised to every school.

label: Hasty Generalization
topic: Should the government cap rent increases?
snippet: One landlord in my street stopped renting after the cap, so rent caps always shrink the housing supply.
why: A single landlord becomes a universal rule.

label: Hasty Generalization
topic: Is a four-day work week better for everyone?
snippet: I was more productive on a four-day week, so everyone will be more productive on one.
why: One person's experience is extended to everyone.

label: Hasty Generalization
topic: Should the voting age be lowered to sixteen?
snippet: A sixteen-year-old once vandalised a bus stop, so teenagers are not ready to vote.
why: One incident stands in for an entire age group.

label: Red Herring
topic: Should the government cap rent increases?
snippet: You ask about rent caps, but the real scandal is that the mayor spent a fortune on bicycle lanes.
why: Switches from rent to an unrelated spending scandal.

label: Red Herring
topic: Should schools ban phones?
snippet: Instead of talking about phones, we should ask why the canteen still serves chips every day.
why: Diverts to canteen food instead of phones.

label: Red Herring
topic: Should AI be allowed to grade essays?
snippet: The critics never mention that the school's roof has leaked for three years.
why: The leaking roof is irrelevant to AI grading.

label: Red Herring
topic: Should cities ban cars from their centres?
snippet: Forget the traffic trial for a moment — what about the council's decision to cancel the fireworks?
why: Asks about fireworks to avoid the traffic trial.

label: Red Herring
topic: Should social platforms verify every user?
snippet: Rather than debating verification, the panel should ask why the platform's chief executive earns so much.
why: Executive pay is unrelated to whether verification works.
